scope: Real elevenid-beta Python passport retirement before the single post-deletion Rust deployment; production is outside this operation
shared_service: Beta issuance is one Python service for passport and unrelated issuance routes. Keep unrelated issuance available; the passport writer is the physical-document job and Flow write surface, not the whole container.

required_identity: exact Python issuance container ID, immutable image digest and Compose labels
PostgreSQL container ID, cluster system identifier and database identity
Gateway and Flow container IDs, image digests and passport owner selectors
the protected main source, signed stack manifest and exact Credentials deletion PR head
authority.reject: Ambiguous or changed identity, production labels, an already active unrelated mutation, or a missing protected release blocks the operation

database_enforcement.ownership: Enumerate every live application and migration database role with write or DDL access to guarded objects. Create a trusted guard owner with NOLOGIN and transfer ownership of the issuance_service and flow_service schemas and three fenced tables away from every live app role. Preserve the schema, table, sequence and function privileges needed for unrelated runtime behavior without granting trigger or guarded-object DDL control. No live app role may own, disable, drop, replace, or bypass fence triggers, functions, or state; verify owners, enabled triggers, memberships and effective grants before and after installation.
database_enforcement.migrations: Before installing the fence, prove a trusted migration path for the later official deployment. A separate privileged migration executor, unavailable to live application containers, may change non-guarded schema objects under the beta deployment lock. Any DDL on guarded tables or schemas must preserve the effective fence, revalidate its definitions and grants before applications restart, and leave it installed until the Rust-owner transition. Before fence mutation, the protected installer requires PASSPORT_BETA_SCHEMA_VALIDATE_ONLY=true in the exact running beta Flow and issuance-native container generation bound to the fenced PostgreSQL route. That mode validates required schema and migration heads without application-role DDL; missing or incompatible schema fails startup. The mode alone is not proof that a fence is installed. Never grant temporary guarded-object DDL to a live app role or run the existing app-role migration unchanged if ownership would make it fail.
database_enforcement.truncate: Revoke TRUNCATE and ownership-derived TRUNCATE from every live application and migration role on the guarded tables, and install a rejecting TRUNCATE trigger for direct and CASCADE paths. Prove rows cannot be discarded by TRUNCATE after fence installation.
database_enforcement.predicate: Guard the exact physical-document job table and physical-document Flow definitions/instances using both OLD and NEW rows. A write to a definitionless instance is denied only when its structure proves physical-document work; unrelated verification writes remain available. The separate conservative drain selector in passport-beta-cutover-drain-behavior.json still counts every other nonterminal definitionless instance except its exact expired synthetic OID4VP orphan shape; those rows block installation or later receipts without being mislabeled as passport writes. Do not deny unrelated defined Flows merely because context text contains the word passport.
database_enforcement.phase_visibility: The atomic install takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE locks on all three guarded tables before the definitive drain counts. Every old writer must commit or roll back before the count; installed triggers and ownership become visible in the same commit. There is no intermediate intake phase.
database_enforcement.tests: Exercise the fence against disposable PostgreSQL with competing transactions, direct application-role writes, DDL and TRUNCATE bypass attempts including CASCADE, physical and unrelated Flow fixtures, and crash/retry behavior before use on beta. A protected CI job must execute these disposable tests rather than skip them.

phases.name: fully_fenced
phases.atomicity: Under the beta deployment lock, one PostgreSQL transaction takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE locks on the passport job and Flow write surfaces, verifies the definitive drain and artifact-format counts, installs the durable full fence and guard ownership, then commits. In-flight work must finish before installation; no intermediate phase accepts bounded writes.
phases.drain: Require zero nonterminal passport jobs, zero legacy or unknown artifacts, zero unreadable artifacts, and zero active physical-document Flows from the identified beta database. Preserve every existing job and artifact; an unresolved row blocks installation.
phases.continuity: Wait for in-flight work before installing the fence. After installation, unrelated issuance routes and non-passport Flow writes remain available. No live Python passport signing fallback is permitted.

phases.name: rust_owner
phases.atomicity: During the later single official aggregate beta deployment, keep the full fence until all old application writers are stopped under the same deployment lock; exact post-deletion Rust images, Gateway/Flow selectors, and the running digest-pinned Credentials issuance image are verified. Prove that the Credentials image lacks the removed Python passport routes before removing or replacing the fence and resuming Rust passport writes; an uncertain cutover remains fail closed.
phases.continuity: No Python passport owner, mixed nine-route owner or production mutation is allowed.

protected_evidence.initial: Attest source-bound beta Compose service/container/image identities, PostgreSQL system identifier and database OID, privileged guard ownership/grants, enabled trigger and function-definition hashes, the transactionally installed full fence epoch, frozen drain query/hash and zero counts, unchanged production resources, and unrelated beta service continuity. Prove a direct passport write is rejected while representative unrelated issuance writes remain possible.
protected_evidence.final: Revise Credentials PR #305's current whole-container-stop verifier and implement its missing protected producer together for this scoped fence; neither existing check can qualify this contract yet. The producer re-inspects the same database and running shared Python container generation, proves the full fence still exists, and attests a strictly later zero-count watermark and the exact Credentials deletion PR head. A changed head or missing fence requires a new final run.
protected_evidence.absence: A deployment mutex, static Compose render, disposable database, zero-count query before the fence, or operator assertion alone is not a retirement receipt.
